title: Burgruine Kronburg Zams
highlights: Dramatically situated castle ruin perched on a steep rocky outcrop high above the Inn valley
Constructed in the late 14th century to guard the upper Inn valley thoroughfare
Combined pilgrimage destination featuring the heritage Kronburg sanctuary and inn
Sweeping panoramic vistas of the Lechtal Alps and the Landeck mountain basin
kurzbeschreibung: The ruins of Burgruine Kronburg perch boldly on a rocky cone above Zams, offering spectacular panoramic views over the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Fortified Guardian over the Inntal

The castle ruins of Burgruine Kronburg rise atop a prominent, steep rocky crag between Zams and Schönwies at an altitude of approximately 1,080 metres. Built from 1380 onward by Heinrich von Starkenberg, the fortress served to secure the upper Inntal and the vital trade routes leading over the Arlberg.

Castle Romance and Pilgrimage Site

From the valley floor, a scenic walking trail winds past the baroque pilgrimage church of Kronburg up to the castle ruins. The preserved perimeter walls, arched windows, and the keep offer an evocative glimpse of medieval architecture against the majestic backdrop of the Lechtaler Alpen.
